subject: starfish
readings: XY panel is the profile (top-down view of the radial body), ZY and XZ show arm thickness/side curvature
top arm tip (12,2) -> vertical arm, length 10
right arm tip (24,12) -> horizontal arm, length 12
left arm tip (0,12) -> horizontal arm, length 12
bottom-right arm tip (16,24) -> diagonal arm, dx=4,dy=12, length ~13
bottom-left arm tip (8,24) -> diagonal arm, dx=-4,dy=12, length ~13
ZY panel shows arm profile with z-thickness ~8 units near hub, tapering to point at tip, consistent with flat radial arms
XZ panel shows hub as a raised dome (z ~8 to ~16) with thin flat arms (z~11-13) extending outward
notes: Starfish has 5-fold radial symmetry, not bilateral, so only two of the five arms form true left/right mirror pairs (arm_R/arm_L and arm_BR/arm_BL); arm_top is unpaired, analogous to a lone anterior arm. No head node: the central disc tapers directly into arms without a distinct neck/head lobe, so it is treated as trunk (root 'disc') per the fused-body rule. No tail present. Each arm is modeled as a single unsegmented limb (hub->tip) since no internal joints are visible in the mesh (arms are smooth, ridged but continuous). Lengths for the mirrored pairs were averaged/assumed equal per the proportion (not pose) rule, using the read tip coordinates as the basis: right/left arms both set to 12 (matching x-extent to grid edges), bottom-left/bottom-right both set to 13 (from diagonal distance sqrt(4^2+12^2)). Directions use the XY-panel screen coordinates with y-sign flipped (screen-down = negative frame-y) per the stated frame convention; dz taken as 0 since ZY-panel cross-section shows arms are essentially planar/flat radiating from the hub, with z-thickness variation only in the hub bulge (not encoded as a separate limb, just body volume).
